key_insight: Robots appear to learn task steps and object roles from demonstrations, rather than just visual appearance. This suggests manipulation knowledge can transfer across scenes, but effective in-context learning must account for the robot’s current environment.
problem_solved: Trained manipulation policies tie skills to their training distribution, while in-context learning has lagged because demonstrations from other scenes lack feedback from the world the robot currently faces.
method: Use in-context demonstrations to guide manipulation rather than relying solely on skills encoded in trained network weights.
Emphasize semantic task structure: which steps to perform and what roles objects play.
Identify current-world feedback as the missing ingredient in learning from demonstrations recorded elsewhere; the truncated abstract does not specify the full mechanism.
impact: This direction could make robot skills easier to reuse across changing environments without retraining for every scene. Implementation details and performance gains cannot be established from the supplied abstract.

paper_title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
paper_authors: Heng Fang, Zehui Guo, Yuehan Zhang, Mingyang Du, Dingkang Liang
